security_audit.summary: Three documented local Python commands are confirmed as external-command actions for initialization, consent lookup, and artifact validation. The remaining 34 detections are false positives from Markdown formatting, fixed documentation links, metadata URLs, and a redirected git error stream. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found in the reviewed content.

remediation.issue: Local Python scripts are executed from a resolved repository root.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit confirmation immediately before each write-capable command, validate the resolved root, and document the expected script checksum or trusted installation source.

remediation.issue: The consent lookup command accepts an aggregate identifier placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Pass identifiers as a separately quoted argument, validate the accepted identifier format, and avoid placing sensitive identifiers in command history or logs.

remediation.issue: Privacy procedures discuss working-tree deletion and history erasure.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run and scope confirmation mandatory, require a protected backup process, and clearly separate routine working-tree erasure from administrator-approved history rewriting.

content.value_statement: Project context becomes difficult to find when notes are scattered or stale. This skill organizes authorized working memory while preserving registry ownership and privacy boundaries.
actual_capabilities: Initialize private runtime memory from repository templates after authorization.
Review HOT, WARM, and COLD notes with source and freshness guidance.
Consolidate duplicate non-canonical notes while preserving conflicts and provenance.
Archive stale working notes with path, hash, and supersession metadata.
Prepare authorized privacy erasure work with dry-run scope reporting.
Create handoff checkpoints without changing canonical registry facts.
limitations: It does not accept, reject, or directly change canonical registry facts.
Persistent writes and purge operations require explicit authorization.
It cannot prove complete erasure from Git history, backups, or external systems.
It depends on project-local templates, registries, and validation scripts.

use_cases.title: Start a new project memory space
use_cases.description: Initialize private memory templates and define the first priorities without storing sensitive production data.

use_cases.title: Prepare a cross-session handoff
use_cases.description: Refresh a compact checkpoint with pending work, source offsets, and the next approved action.
use_cases.target_user: Developer using an AI coding assistant

use_cases.title: Review an erasure request
use_cases.description: Plan a scoped privacy purge, identify affected working notes, and report limitations before any authorized deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize private project memory from the templates. Show the proposed paths and ask for approval before writing.

prompt_templates.title: Review current context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our HOT and WARM memory. List current priorities, stale notes, and the source record for each conclusion.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate duplicates
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicate non-canonical notes for this campaign. Propose a consolidation plan that preserves conflicts and source references.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a privacy purge
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a dry-run plan to erase the pseudonymous subject ID Subject-A1B2 from authorized working memory. Show scope and request confirmation before changes.

output_examples.input: Review project memory for stale context.
output: HOT: 4 active priorities with source pointers.
WARM: 2 notes are older than 90 days and need review.

output_examples.input: Prepare a consolidation plan for duplicate notes.
output: Two non-canonical notes cover the same observation window.
Keep the newer note as primary and retain the older note with a supersession reference.

best_practices: Ask for explicit approval before the first persistent write.
Store source references and observation dates with every durable note.
Treat HOT memory as an index and verify important facts in live registry records.
anti_patterns: Do not store credentials, raw contact data, or production exports in templates.
Do not treat cached notes as proof of current consent or canonical truth.
Do not delete ambiguous records without a confirmed scope and authority.

faq.question: Does this skill replace a project database?
faq.answer: No. It manages working notes and pointers. Registry event streams remain the canonical source of facts.

faq.question: Can it write memory automatically?
faq.answer: Only when the current request explicitly authorizes the persistent write. Read-only review and dry runs need no write approval.

faq.question: What are HOT, WARM, and COLD notes?
faq.answer: HOT holds small current pointers, WARM holds active evidence, and COLD holds older historical material.

faq.question: Can it delete personal data?
faq.answer: It can plan and perform authorized working-memory erasure. It cannot guarantee deletion from history, backups, or external systems.

faq.question: Does it change registry facts?
faq.answer: No. It routes conflicts and proposed changes to the registry owner.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible hosts.
